item.title: NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION
item.description:
Citywide Administrative Services | Special Materials | Notice | Flagged: Special Materials (non-routine) In plain English (machine-written): On Oct. 14, 2026, the city's chief procurement officer approved a request from the Department of Citywide Administrative Services that acknowledged the agency missed a two-day deadline to notify two low bidders that their bids were non-responsive for a contract to buy asphalt rollers, and the award went ahead to the next qualified bidder.

On October 14, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB Rules), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Citywide Administrative in connection with a Competitive Sealed Bid solicitation for Rollers, Asphalt DOT, EPIN 85726B0029002.

The minor rules violation occurred when the Agency failed to notify the two lowest bidders of its determination that their bids were non-responsive within the two-day period required under Section 2-07 of the PPB Rules. This oversight did not affect the evaluation of bids, compromise the integrity of the procurement process, or alter the determination to award the contract to the next lowest responsive and responsible bidder. Upon identifying the violation, the Agency notified the affected bidders and proceeded with the award in accordance with the PPB Rules.
